summary.going_well: The agent disclosed its AI identity and recording notice at opening <ref job="SRJ_fze6zMLGVkNC" item="item_467ed93f-235">before conducting intake</ref>. Across the tested purchase, refinance, and home-equity paths, it reached the soft-credit-review versus summary choice without choosing for the borrower <ref job="SRJ_fze6zMLGVkNC" item="item_1a2b7dbe-c00">in the purchase path</ref> <ref job="SRJ_gB9N5h7iwUR5" item="item_575b03f5-72b">and the refinance path</ref>.
summary.to_improve: First, qualify the repeated conventional-refinance claims so borrowers are not given misleading product information. Ensure the HELOC flow asks about variable-rate comfort, then remove financial judgments from intake acknowledgments.

issues.description: In both refinance conversations, the agent asserted that conventional refinancing has <ref job="SRJ_9FwMSDgRWVzQ" item="item_ebbd180f-69d">“no upfront government fees, no permanent mortgage insurance once you reach 20% equity, and higher loan limits”</ref>, repeating the claim <ref job="SRJ_gB9N5h7iwUR5" item="item_8b37b0c8-903">to another borrower</ref>. These categorical product claims can mislead because insurance requirements, costs, and loan limits depend on the loan and borrower.
issues.suggestion: Replace the canned conventional-refinance benefits with qualified, institution-neutral explanations; route borrower-specific insurance, fees, and limits to the licensed loan officer.
issues.label: Product accuracy

issues.description: The HELOC agent moved from saying <ref job="SRJ_3ZPqJeiavD8U" item="item_4d86b87d-c95">rates are typically variable to asking whether the overall structure made sense</ref>, without the required direct question about comfort with a variable rate. This was observed once.
issues.suggestion: Add a required HELOC discovery checkpoint asking explicitly whether the borrower is comfortable with a variable rate before advancing to the disclosure or final choice.
issues.label: Missed question

issues.description: The agent repeatedly assessed borrowers’ finances instead of acknowledging them neutrally, calling debt <ref job="SRJ_rDt9u5kPhmpn" item="item_33098b02-72a">“manageable”</ref> and savings <ref job="SRJ_fze6zMLGVkNC" item="item_b86dd1e3-ad7">“a strong position to be in”</ref>; it also called HELOC debt <ref job="SRJ_3ZPqJeiavD8U" item="item_63960bce-637">“very manageable”</ref>. Such language implies an assessment before the review.
issues.suggestion: Replace evaluative intake acknowledgments with neutral phrases such as “Thank you, I’ve noted that,” and leave financial assessments to the review or loan officer.
issues.label: Judgmental framing
